<issue>
Directory deletion not cascading to child file records in index
## Summary

When a **subdirectory containing source files** is deleted from the project, CodeGraph fails to detect the change and does not update the SQLite index. The deleted files remain in the database, and index counts (files, nodes, edges) stay unchanged.

This appears to be a **cascade deletion bug**: removing a parent directory does not trigger removal of its child file records from the index.

## Reproduction Steps

1. `codegraph init` — initialize index
2. Create nested source file: `docs/1/2/新建文件夹/_0204_.py`
3. Wait for CodeGraph to sync (check `Last Sync` timestamp)
4. **Delete the subdirectory `docs/1`** (which contains `_0204_.py`)
5. Observe: index counts unchanged, deleted file still appears in queries

## Attachment: Diagnostic Tool

I built a lightweight real-time monitor (`codegraph_state.js`) to visualize this bug. It displays live index counts alongside filesystem events, making the mismatch immediately obvious.

**Author: feel free to use or adapt this tool for debugging.**

[codegraph_state.js](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30005409/codegraph_state.js)

</issue>

The repository is at /testbed.

input.instruction: In /testbed, find the file watcher / sync code that handles filesystem change events and removal of files from the index (e.g. watcher, sync, removeFile, deleteFile, unlink, unlinkDir). Report file paths, line numbers and relevant code for how deleted directories are handled (esp. when a directory is deleted and only a directory event arrives, or the watcher uses native fs.watch).

content.content: {"summary":"The watcher is src/sync/watcher.ts, which uses Node's native fs.watch directly. It has two strategies: a recursive watcher on macOS/Windows and one watch per directory on Linux. A deleted directory produces only a directory-name event, and that event is dropped rather than turned into index removals. Actual removal of files from the index happens later in the extraction sync reconcile step, which checks the filesystem for every tracked file.","findings":["src/sync/watcher.ts:414-420: macOS/Windows path. A single fs.watch(projectRoot, {recursive:true}) forwards every event's filename to handleChange(normalizePath(filename)) with no stat check, so a deleted directory name reaches handleChange.","src/sync/watcher.ts:432-436 and 449-497: Linux path (startPerDirectory -> watchTree). One fs.watch per non-ignored directory (watchImpl(dir,{persistent:true}) at line 469) calls handleDirEvent(dir, filename).","src/sync/watcher.ts:520-536 handleDirEvent: computes full=path.join(dir, filename) and calls fs.statSync(full). If it is a directory, it calls watchTree to add a watch. If statSync throws (the path was deleted), the catch at line 534 falls through to handleChange with the deleted path. There is no removal of the deleted directory's watch or pending entries here.","src/sync/watcher.ts:546-562 handleChange: returns early for ignored paths (isAlwaysIgnored, ignoreMatcher) and for non-source files (line 554, isSourceFile). A deleted directory name has no source extension, so it is silently dropped and no pendingFiles entry or sync is scheduled. Deleted source files are not stat-checked here, so their events do pass through to pendingFiles (lines 556-563) and scheduleSync.","src/sync/watcher.ts:568-578 unwatchDir: closes and deletes a dirWatchers entry. It is called only from the fs.watch 'error' handler (line 494), never when a watched directory is deleted. Watches for deleted directories therefore persist in dirWatchers until an error occurs.","src/sync/watcher.ts:763-800 flush: sync runs via syncFn; pendingFiles entries are removed only after a successful sync whose lastSeenMs <= syncStartedMs (lines 790-793). There is no explicit removal path for deleted files in the watcher itself.","src/extraction/index.ts:2485-2510 (sync reconcile): removals are detected by walking trackedFiles and checking `!currentSet.has(path) || !fs.existsSync(path.join(rootDir, path))`. Matching rows are removed with queries.deleteFile (line 2507) after incoming cross-file edges are resurrected (lines 2490-2505). This is what actually removes deleted files and deleted-directory children from the index, and it runs on the next sync, which the watcher triggers only from a source-file event.","src/extraction/index.ts:2225-2255 (indexing a changed file): an existing file is deleted with queries.deleteFile(filePath) at line 2253 before re-extraction, after snapshotting cross-file incoming edges (issue #899).","src/extraction/index.ts:1124-1127 getChangedFiles / git path: git 'D' status entries are pushed to deleted unfiltered (line 1127). src/extraction/index.ts:2605-2618 turns those into removed[] only when the path is already tracked. Lines 2661-2667 do the same for non-git scans (tracked files missing from currentFiles).","Gap: a deleted directory whose files were removed one at a time is handled through each child file's event from the directory's own watch. A directory-only deletion event with no child events is dropped, so index cleanup for that directory depends on the next reconcile sync (extraction/index.ts:2490). The stale inotify watch for the deleted directory is also not released (watcher.ts:494 is only on error)."],"confidence":0.7}
